analysis.investment_thesis: Parmeshwar Metal is a sub-scale copper scrap recycler with a 0.20% ROE — a commodity-processing business with no discernible moat and returns that destroy capital versus India's ~7% risk-free rate. A 12x P/E on near-zero earnings is not "cheap"; it is a statistical mirage on a tiny balance sheet.
key_strengths: High promoter holding at 72.03% signals skin in the game
Operates in a recyclable/ESG-aligned copper circularity niche
Debt-free enough to still post a (tiny) profit at P/E 12
key_risks: ROE of 0.20% — capital is effectively idle vs. 7% G-Sec
Pure commodity spread business (scrap vs. LME copper) — no pricing power
Zero institutional ownership (FII 0%, DII 0.03%) = no price discovery
red_flags: ROE of 0.20% is far below Munger's 15% threshold — this is not a quality business
Incorporated only in 2016; no multi-cycle track record through a copper downturn
Micro-cap (189 Cr) with negligible institutional sponsorship — liquidity and governance risk
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Inversion first: what would make this a bad investment? A commodity recycler earning sub-1% on equity, selling a fungible product (copper rod/wire) into a market where LME sets the price and scrap availability sets the cost. That describes Parmeshwar exactly. A 0.20% ROE means management is converting shareholder capital into almost nothing — you'd do 35x better owning a Government of India bond. In my mental model of business quality, this is the opposite of a compounding machine; it is a capital trap dressed up as an industrial.

The 12x P/E looks optically reasonable until you realize it is 12x a vanishing "E." Multiplied out, the earnings yield on equity is ~0.2%, and any working-capital expansion to grow revenue will require more capital earning those same pathetic returns — the definition of a business that gets worse as it grows. High promoter holding is the only genuine positive, but promoter alignment cannot manufacture a moat where none exists. I'd pass without hesitation and spend the time reading about a business I can actually understand and admire.
